Results.ReviewText:
While the initial sticker shock for the grill may not immediately have you racing to put it in your cart, I can reassure you it's worth it.  Having friends and family who have over the years been burned (not literally) by cheaper grills only lasting 2-3 years, I didn't want the same outcome.  I knew I'd have to spend some money to get the appropriate quality for a grill that quite frankly gets used everyday.  And if I do end up having issues, I can rest easy knowing it's backed by a manufacturer 10 year warranty - something that certainly makes it easier to sleep at night.  Having used this grill for a few weeks now, I love it. Just make sure to do your research and take care of this BEFORE even using it.  The grates need 'seasoned' before first use, and using grill spray (anti-stick) is highly recommended since you are on bare cast iron, not your typical coated grates.  While this can be a pain, I assure you with proper use, it's much more efficient and if properly cared for will have a lifespan much longer than coated grates.  
My only gripe with this grill is the igniter seems to be finicky (as is the story with any grill, right?).  It has lit every single time, however sometimes it will take longer - at times up to 10 seconds.  I would think at this price point I'd get immediate ignition every single time.  However, this is definitely not a big enough issue to not make this worthy of your backyard.
Results.Title: Great grill, worth the price

Results.ReviewText: Great gas grill for my husband and me. We’re not frequent nor “seasoned” grillers, on average we grill a few times during the warm weather months in the Midwest, so this Sprit II model is a perfect investment for our first grill. We absolutely love it. It heats up quickly, enough cooking space for a smaller household, it has hooks to hang your grilling tools on the side, and the fuel gauge that lets you know when you’re running low on your gas tank is one of the reasons why we bought it. My only gripe is that the cast iron grates are hard to clean (as all iron grates are), but we’ll probably buy the chrome grates that are an option for this model so that will elevate the problem somewhat. We have a medium sized patio, so it fits nicely.  Also, we invested in Weber’s grill cover to protect it from the elements. Unfortunately, they discontinued the red color grill lid for this model which is the one I wanted for a pop of color on my patio, but we bought it anyway in black, and love it!

Photos.Caption: Lid paint, enamel and flare damage
Cracked off front panel support screw housing

Results.ReviewText:
This grill was bought at the end of the 2019 grilling season, after much research, for the Weber quality that I have experienced in the past with my Kettle Charcoal BBQ, and for the heat efficiency that Weber bbqs are also known for.  Additionally I liked the available colour options.  

When I received the BBQ, I inspected the packaging closely, and found no shipping damage.  This is significant since I didn't plan to assemble the BBQ until the 2020 grilling season, and the BBQ would remain in the box throughout the winter months. 

Therefore, I was extremely surprised to find what appeared to be production defects and other damage. 

1. The most significant was the damage to the grilling box.  The grilling box was cracked at the front edges, in nearly identical ways on both the front left and right side corners.  

2. The front edge of the lid, on the right side and BEHIND the lid handle was flared out, and the paint and enamel was severely chipped and cracked.  

3. There were dents on the supports, and the flanges of the leg parts were bent, making assembly difficult

4. One of the supporting screw receptors for the right-most burner dial was broken off

I am amazed that a product with obvious defects would be packaged so carefully in the box.  There was no damage to the exterior packaging, and none to the internal cardboard protection packaging (which is some of the strongest that I've ever seen).  That fact, and also the oddly protected locations of some of the biggest points of damage (behind the handle, at the front edges of the grill box) indicate that this grill was either not produced to standard, or was damaged prior to shipping. 

I am honestly surprised at what I have here, and more so at the volume of other reviews that appear to indicate similar experiences by others purchasers of this product.  

Winning reviews is one thing, but if a product cannot perform as reviewed, or as intended, or requires lengthy customer service intervention just to get to the point that you thought you were at when you purchased, then value is being lost.  Quality control matters.
Results.Title: Not the Weber Quality I was expecting
